import csv, json, re

INV = "/app/input/seller_book_sections.csv"
rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(INV)))

# Required disclosure classes (amended list = 9 from sec 2 + marital status + source of income per 5a)
REQUIRED = ["race","color","religion","sex","familial status","national origin",
            "disability","sexual orientation","veteran status","marital status","source of income"]

# Proxy / protected-class term detection in PROSE (outside the notice).
# Per sec 2 + proxies: houses of worship, parish/faith schools, street-by-kind-of-household,
# plus the bare class terms themselves.
PROXY_PATTERNS = [
    (r"\bchurch(es)?\b","religion"),
    (r"\bchurchgoing\b","religion"),
    (r"\bparish\b","religion"),
    (r"\bcongregation\b","religion"),
    (r"\bfaith community\b","religion"),
    (r"\bfaith school\b","religion"),
    (r"\bhouse(s)? of worship\b","religion"),
    (r"\bfamily-oriented\b","familial status"),
    (r"\bchurchgoing households\b","familial status"),
    (r"\byoung families\b","familial status"),
    (r"\blong-established families\b","familial status"),
]

NOTICE_RE = re.compile(r"This brokerage complies with.*?(?:veteran status|source of income|familial status|national origin|sex)[^.]*\.")

def classes_in_notice(text):
    m = re.search(r"This brokerage complies with(.*)", text, re.S)
    if not m:
        return None, None
    notice = "This brokerage complies with" + m.group(1)
    found = []
    low = notice.lower()
    for c in REQUIRED:
        # match class as a phrase
        if re.search(r"\b"+re.escape(c)+r"\b", low):
            found.append(c)
    return found, notice

RESPONSIBLE = {"closing_page","agent_bio"}

# Personal-narrative solicitation phrases (love letter)
PN_PHRASES = [
    "write us a letter about what brought you here",
    "tell us about yourselves",
    "send a personal note about yourself",
    "include a short personal note about themselves",
    "include a covering letter introducing yourself",
    "the sellers would like to know who is buying",
    "we invite buyers to include a short personal note about themselves",
    "the one that moves us most is the one we will take",
]

def prose_outside_notice(body, notice):
    if notice is None:
        return body
    return body.replace(notice," ")

results = {}
for r in rows:
    sid = r["section_id"]; role = r["role"]; body = r["body"]
    found_classes, notice = classes_in_notice(body)
    has_notice = notice is not None
    compliant = has_notice and all(c in found_classes for c in REQUIRED)
    abridged = has_notice and not compliant

    flags = []
    # sec 1 personal narrative
    pn = any(p in body.lower() for p in PN_PHRASES)
    if pn:
        flags.append("PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE")

    # sec 2 protected class language
    pcl = False
    # protected-class terms IN THE NOTICE are exempt only if compliant (sec 3)
    if has_notice:
        if not compliant:
            # abridged or partial -> notice terms count (no exemption)
            # notice always names at least some protected classes
            notice_low = notice.lower()
            for c in REQUIRED[:9]:  # the 9 sec-2 protected classes
                if re.search(r"\b"+re.escape(c)+r"\b", notice_low):
                    pcl = True
        # if compliant, notice terms are exempt -> don't count them
    # protected-class terms in PROSE (outside notice) are NEVER exempt
    prose = prose_outside_notice(body, notice)
    for pat,_ in PROXY_PATTERNS:
        if re.search(pat, prose, re.I):
            pcl = True
    # also bare class terms in prose
    for c in REQUIRED[:9]:
        if re.search(r"\b"+re.escape(c)+r"\b", prose.lower()):
            pcl = True
    if pcl:
        flags.append("PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE")

    # sec 4 disclaimer missing (responsible roles only)
    if role in RESPONSIBLE:
        if not has_notice or abridged:
            flags.append("DISCLAIMER_MISSING")

    finding = "|".join(flags) if flags else "none"
    results[sid] = finding

# Fair-housing audit memo — seller's book

**Prepared for:** Legal sign-off, pre-print
**Standard applied:** RE-FH-9 (Real-estate marketing collateral fair-housing standard), **including the 2026 amendments at §5**
**Source inventory:** `input/seller_book_sections.csv` (30 sections)
**Deliverables:** `fairhousing_audit.csv` (per-section findings), `fairhousing_memo.md` (this memo), `results.json` (counts for the sign-off form)

> The book has not fully caught up to the 2026 amendments, so the audit was run against the amended standard, not against the paragraphs currently in the manuscript. That is the source of most of the findings below.

---

## 1. How the rules were applied

RE-FH-9 defines three findings, plus `none`. A section can carry more than one; where it does, they are joined with `|` in the fixed order `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE | PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE | DISCLAIMER_MISSING`.

**§1 — Personal-narrative solicitation (`PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`).** A section that solicits or presents a buyer "love letter" or similar personal narrative tied to buyer identity is flagged, **whatever its role**. I treated any invitation for the buyer to write about themselves / their story / who is buying as a love-letter solicitation.

**§2 — Protected-class language (`PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`).** The classes the standard protects are: race, colour, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status. **Proxies count the same as bare terms**: naming houses of worship / parish or faith schools, or describing a street by the kind of household that lives on it, reaches religion and familial status respectively. I flagged phrases such as "churches", "churchgoing", "parish", "congregation", "faith community", "family-oriented street", "young families", "long-established families", "households". (The standard spells the class "colour"; the manuscript spells it "color". I counted "color" as satisfying the "colour" requirement.)

**§3 — Mandated-disclosure exception (exemption from §2 only).** A section that carries the fair-housing *notice* is exempt from §2 **for the notice text** only if that notice names **every** class the disclosure is required to name (see the required list below). Two narrow limits:
- An **abridged** notice (some, not all, required classes) earns **no exemption at all** — every protected-class term it names counts toward §2.
- The exemption covers **§2 and nothing else**; §1 (personal narrative) and §4 (disclaimer) still apply on their own terms.
- Protected-class terms a section uses **in its own prose, outside the notice, are never exempt**.

**§4 — Required disclaimer (`DISCLAIMER_MISSING`).** Only sections in a **responsible role** are assessed here. As drafted the responsible role is `closing_page`; **§5b extends it to `agent_bio`**. A responsible section that carries no notice, or an abridged one, is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. Sections in any other role (`listing_copy`, `seller_letter`, `disclosure_block`) are **not** assessed for §4, even if they happen to carry (or omit) a notice.

### Required disclosure class list (11 classes)
Per §2 plus the **§5a** additions, a compliant notice must name **all** of:
race, colour, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, **marital status**, **source of income**.

A notice omitting **either** marital status or source of income is abridged for both §3 and §4, however many of the other nine it lists. This is the single biggest source of findings, because the "standing disclosure paragraph" still in circulation (9 classes) predates the amendment.

---

|---|---|

| `protected_lang_count` (finding includes `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`) | 14 |
| `disclaimer_missing_count` (finding includes `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`) | 11 |

The 8 clean sections (`none`): SEC-01, SEC-06, SEC-10, SEC-13, SEC-18, SEC-20, SEC-26, SEC-28.

Counts count **sections**, not labels; a section carrying multiple labels is counted once in `flagged_count` and once in each label's count.
